Restated section 1(c)(i) sets the end of the divestment permission for any person listed in the Annex at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on June 3, 2022. Read with the restated section 1(c) lead-in, which permits the covered divestment purchases and sales before the stated times, the permission for Annex persons lapsed at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on June 3, 2022. Only this transitional permission ended; the section 1(a) prohibition continues, as the held eCFR text of 31 CFR 586.201 shows, and the permission for persons determined after the order in restated section 1(c)(ii) continues to run from each determination.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 14032 (June 3, 2021, 86 FR 30145) expands the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959, replaces and supersedes sections 1 through 5 of Executive Order 13959 with restated sections prohibiting United States persons from purchasing or selling publicly traded securities of listed and determined persons in the military-industrial complex and surveillance technology sectors of the People's Republic of China, replaces the Annex, renumbers section 6 and revokes Executive Order 13974. The order is operative on 2026-10-14. It depends on the national emergency that Executive Order 13959 declared and this order expanded; the held Presidential notices of November 9, 2021 (86 FR 62711), November 8, 2022 (87 FR 68017), November 3, 2023 (88 FR 76987), November 7, 2024 (89 FR 88869) and November 5, 2025 (90 FR 50739) continue it year by year, each recites that Executive Order 14032 amended Executive Order 13959 and revoked Executive Order 13974, and the last continues the emergency beyond November 12, 2025, a date after the cutoff. The held eCFR text of 31 CFR 586.201, 586.106, 586.404 and the part 586 authority citation, checked as of 2026-10-14, implements Executive Order 13959 as amended by this order. One clause ended: the restated section 1(c)(i) divestment permission for Annex persons lapsed by its own terms on June 3, 2022. The Federal Register disposition information for this order records only that it supersedes Executive Order 13959 in part, and the held texts contain no later instrument that revokes, amends or supersedes this order; Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025, a general policy order on criminal regulatory offenses, does not name this order and does not end any clause.

savings.reason: The order is not terminated, so no residual effect after an ending arises. The one ended clause, the restated section 1(c)(i) divestment permission, leaves the section 1(a) prohibition in force and creates no surviving right. The order contains no savings clause that preserves a measure beyond a revocation; restated section 1(d) applies the prohibitions notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits. The bounded searches found no later instrument that revokes or supersedes the order or preserves part of it.
